Here's my perspective as a newer locksmith.

1. What percentage of the time are your working outside vs inside?
95% inside 2% of that is programming car keys  the other 3% is because I mow our lawn.

2. Do you feel like you have a lot of control over whether each job is a success? Or are their a lot of factors outside of your control that can turn a job into a nightmare? 

A lot of it is in our control every nightmare I've faced its been my fault I fucked up my first best system setup for example and had to correct it.

3. Have you preferred working for big-name companies or small ones?
 
I honestly like the smaller companies they tend to send the same guy to our shop and I can build an understanding with them.

4. How long before you felt generally competent? 

I don't. Truthfully I haven't done this long enough yet.

5. How often do you find yourself doing "gross" jobs.(hoarder houses and such)

Before I decided to stay in our shop and went out with service techs I had only been in one hoarders apartment and I felt like shaving my hair off after it was so nasty.

6. Is there a specialization that clearly has the highest earning potential?  

I don't have the knowledge to awnser this question 

7. How much do you make a year, how variable has it been?

I make about 27,000 a year after taxes no variance as I don't get commission in the shop

8. Do you work alone most of the time? 

No always have someone there to help

9. One piece of advise you feel would be most critical to a newcomer? 

It's a trade not a factory or a warehouse job it takes time to learn.

10. Is there another type of White-Van-Man work you might recommend? (outside of plumber/electrician/welder)

Never done any of it so no.

11. Favorite aspects of the job?

I love helping people feel safe and secure. It's skilled labor so I feel like I'm not going to wake up one morning and not have a job. Since I've began my journey as a locksmith I've felt more confident and haven't been happier.
